data.description:
## Summary

Carved out of bug `unhelping-creviced-rhino` (`e127-a3ad-895a-4a2f`), which routed the CLI
`--output json` emitters through the JS-safe decimal-string wire form and pinned that behaviour
with regression tests over **six measured commands** (`show`, `list`, `ready`, `sign`,
`verify-signature`, `audit show`, plus `review-plan --status` and the `--output llm` projections).

That is genuine coverage of those commands. It is **not** coverage of e127's AC "so the CLI
surface cannot drift silently": a CLI command added *later* that emits a bare 19-digit
`time.time_ns()` integer passes today by never being looked at. That is the never-ran failure
class — the suite is green because the new surface is outside its enumeration, not because the
new surface is correct.

e127 could not absorb this work: it was already flagged by the Gerrit `bugfix-size-attestation`
gate at 160 non-test lines (floor 150), and adding a guard plus its tests would both re-trigger
that block and — by widening e127's recorded `file_impact` — stale the plan-review attestation
that cleared it. Split, not deferred.

## The defect

There is no mechanical check that a CLI command emitting JSON to stdout routes through
`rebar._mcp_errors.js_safe_dumps` (or otherwise keeps out-of-JS-safe-range integers off the
wire). The only thing standing between a new command and a silently float64-rounded audit
timestamp is an author remembering.

RFC 8259 §6 guarantees numeric agreement only inside `[-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1]`. e127's RCA
reproduced the harm at runtime: a stored `1787860170488898642` returns from `node`'s plain
`JSON.parse` as `1787860170488898600` — silently 42 ns wrong.

## Proposed shape

`scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py`, wired into `make lint` alongside the sibling guards
(`check_raw_git_writes.py`, `check_tickets_boundary.py`, `check_config_reads.py`).

**Enumerate commands STRUCTURALLY, not from a hand-maintained list.** A literal list of command
names inside the guard reproduces exactly the drift problem it exists to solve, one level up: the
next command is missing from the list for the same reason it is missing from the tests. Derive the
command set from the CLI's own dispatch/parser registry, so a newly registered command is in scope
the moment it is registered.

Suggested mechanism (deterministic, AST): for each in-scope CLI module, flag any `json.dumps` /
`_json.dumps` whose result flows into `print(...)` or `sys.stdout.write(...)`, with a teaching
message naming `js_safe_dumps`. Fail-closed on an argv/expression it cannot resolve, per
`check_raw_git_writes.py`'s established convention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py` exists and is wired into `make lint`.
- [ ] **NEGATIVE CONTROL (the load-bearing one): the guard FLAGS a deliberately-seeded new CLI
      command that emits a bare out-of-JS-safe-range integer to stdout.** A test asserts the
      guard's non-zero exit and the offending location on that seeded tree. A guard that only ever
      passes has proven nothing — this criterion is what makes the rest non-vacuous.
- [ ] The guard PASSES on the clean tree (exit 0), so it is not merely tripping on everything.
- [ ] The in-scope command set is derived from the CLI's dispatch/parser registry, NOT from a
      literal list of command names maintained inside the guard. A test proves a newly registered
      command enters scope without editing the guard.
- [ ] The guard is deterministic and provider-neutral: no CI-system-specific trigger, no network,
      no LLM (`make lint` must run it anywhere, per the `project.portability` criterion).

## Notes / scope

- Out of scope: `rebar export` NDJSON, tracked separately as `guilty-pusslike-wyvern`
  (`a8db-dc3c-983a-40b0`) — a separately versioned interop projection with a `rebar import`
  round-trip contract.
- Out of scope: the MCP surface, which is guarded structurally already by
  `install_js_safe_guard` rebinding `mcp.tool`, so every registered tool is wrapped by
  construction rather than by enumeration.
data.title: No structural guard stops a NEW CLI command from emitting bare >2^53 ns integers
